hypotheses.reasoning: The first anomaly shows up at 02:49 in enrichment-svc: calls to the third-party geo-IP provider (api.geoip.example) got slow, taking 5.3s and then 11.2s (#152, #156). From 02:50 they failed with 30s upstream timeouts (#165, #172, #175). Each of those timeouts made ingest-api's EnrichClient.enrich time out after 30s on the same trace (#166, #173, #176). Those 30s waits filled ingest-api's 50-connection pool to enrichment-svc, and requests then hit checkout timeouts (#178, #188, #192). The gateway started returning 503s on POST /v1/events from 02:52 (#177 onward). geo-cache, events-db and event-processor all look healthy, and there were no deploys. The earlier 400 (#44) is just a client validation error and unrelated.

The dependency that failed is an external provider, so this may be an outage on their side. The logs only show timeouts, though, with no 5xx or connection-refused errors from the provider and no status-page notice, so the timeout reading fits the evidence better.
Pool saturation in ingest-api spread the failure to the gateway, but that spread is a consequence of the geo-IP timeouts, not the cause.

verdict.recommendedAction: Put a short timeout (about 2s) and a circuit breaker on the geo-IP provider calls in enrichment-svc. When the provider is slow, skip geo enrichment and fall back to geo-cache only. Cut ingest-api's enrichment timeout well below 30s, or make enrichment asynchronous so it can't block ingestion. Check the geo-IP provider's status and escalate to the vendor.
